text:
maya: Heads up — canary rollout v1.12.3 hit a perf regression on small-chat. p50 up ~12%, p95 up ~18%. Canary paused by release-ops. CI perf job flagged it this morning :eyes:
ci-bot: perf-check failed for commit 0a1b2c3 (v1.12.3). Threshold breach: small-chat.p95 > baseline by 18%. See job: https://ci/internal/jobs/4321
jon: ouch. any quick profiling traces?
samir: ran a short flamegraph and kernel-selection trace. Looks like commit 0a1b2c3 replaced the old tile planner for matmul with the new auto-tiler. On our common sequence lengths, that caused the runtime to pick a different GEMM kernel (fallback slower path) for sequences <128. Also batching heuristics ended up splitting requests more often — effective batch sizes dropped 20%.
lee: interesting — does KV cache play into this? we saw cache hit-rate dip in the canary telemetry.
samir: yes. two things combined: smaller micro-batches increased KV cache churn because requests that would have been coalesced now had interleaved prefixes, so cache key locality dropped. I measured KV hit-rate decline from 93% -> 78% in the worst buckets. That amplifies token compute work and adds latency.
jon: can you paste the bisect/commands you used?
samir: git bisect pointed to 0a1b2c3 -> the tiler change. Repro steps I used locally:
```
# reproduce perf run
./tools/perf/run_microbench.py --workload small-chat --model gpt-like --iters 120 \
  --trace kernel-selection --batcher-config configs/batcher/default.yaml
```
And to capture kernel selection logs: set ENV DEBUG_KERNEL_SELECT=1 and collect /tmp/kernel-trace.log
jon: ok that gives us a repro and a root cause. thoughts on mitigation? revert or patch?
maya: we'll need a fast mitigation for the canary. revert the tiler commit from the release branch to unblock rollout. Meanwhile, samir, can you open a follow-up PR that tightens the tiler decision rules for short sequences and respects the legacy kernel override?
samir: yes. I'm drafting a PR that: 1) restores explicit override for small sequence GEMM kernel, 2) tweaks batching window to prefer coalescing under low-latency workloads, 3) adds a toggle flag to enable the new tiler per-model.
lee: also we should harden CI so this doesn't slip. Current perf tests are noisy and we only run microbench once on each PR. I recommend adding:
- a KV-cache specific microbenchmark that measures hit-rate and latency for representative prefix mixes
- run perf tests 3x and use median to reduce flakiness
- tighten thresholds for small-chat p50/p95 to 5%/8% respectively (from current 10%/15%)
jon: agree. add a gating CI job that runs the critical microbench suite for merge to release branch. If KV-hit drops by >5% or p95 regresses >8% fail the merge.
maya: action items:
- maya: coordinate revert on release branch (in progress)
- samir: open PR with tiler fixes + test coverage (ETA 6h)
- lee: add KV-hit microbenchmark and median-of-3 runs to perf CI (ETA 1 day)
- jon: adjust release gating thresholds and add notification for canary stalls (ETA 4h)
ci-bot: deploy/rollback: canary paused for v1.12.3 by maya at 2026-03-18T10:12Z
jon: one more meta thing — let's add a small integration test that simulates interleaved prefixes to catch KV churn regressions. Make it fast (<30s) and run in PR-level perf suite.
samir: adding that to the PR too. I'll include the kernel-selection trace in the PR for easier review.
maya: thanks all — good catch by CI. Once revert is in we'll re-run canary and monitor KV hit-rate + latency. :thumbsup:
